messages:
maria: Heads up — while onboarding quantized v2-small on 64k context I see subtle generational drift when we use cached KV vs full-prefill. Not a huge token error but enough to fail our goldset checks. Posting quick reproducer and logs.

maria: Repro steps: 
```
# start server with quant4 kernel
./run_infer --model v2-small-q4 --max-context 65536 --enable-kv-cache
# send long prompt (attached) then generate 512 tokens incremental
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d @long_prompt.json
```

maria: Key observation: when we prefill full context and then continue, outputs match baseline. When we stream tokens and rely on incremental KV updates we drift after ~1200 tokens. Error looks like small probability mass shift; manifests as token substitutions at boundary.

kevin: Can you paste a short diff of token sequences where they diverge?

maria: Sure — baseline vs incremental at first divergence point: 
```
baseline: "...the committee concluded that the policy was..."
incremental: "...the committee concluded it the policy was..."
```
small but triggers rouge/regression.

ash: Did you try forcing fp16 kernels for rotary math vs the int8/int4 path? Might be a quant-kernel order or accumulation issue.

maria: Yes — switching runtime to fp16 fixes the divergence. So likely quant kernel or int accumulation / rotation scaling mismatch.

sam: Do we have a unit test that compares prefill vs incremental outputs across different quant levels? If not we should add one to catch this.

maria: Not for longctx+streaming; current tests are <8k. I ran a quick script locally that replays the same token ops in both modes and diffs logits; attaching log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] layer 10 rotary_scale mismatch: max_delta=8.3e-04 mean=2.1e-05
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] layer 23 kv_write_drop detected at idx=4096
```

kevin: kv_write_drop sounds like we may be clipping or misaligning indices when we shard or compact caches. Are you running multi-shard?

maria: Single GPU for this run. I checked offsets — prefill path writes k/v sequentially; incremental uses memcpy with stride optimizations. Could be an int4 alignment rounding bug.

ash: Worth checking rotary frequency scaling: some quant kernels precompute sin/cos with reduced precision; if we apply a different scaling factor or rounding between prefill vs incremental, phases drift. Search for any double->float casts around the ropemap code.

sam: I'll add a smoke test to CI that runs a short long-context replay with both modes on quant4 and compares top-10 tokens. If divergence > threshold, fail. Will open PR.

ci-bot: CI ticket created: https://repo.internal/redwood/infra/issues/4207 — longctx prefill vs incremental quant4 test (sam)

maria: Thanks. Meanwhile I tried a quick mitigation: when incremental write path sees alignment != 64 bytes we fall back to elementwise copy. That reduced errors but didn't eliminate them.

kevin: Could this be a stride/pack transient where the tail of a packed tile is reused incorrectly? Any CCRs in memcpy util recently?

maria: We updated the pack util last month for performance. Reverting to old memcpy removes divergence on my machine. So pack util likely culprit — specifically the tail-handling code for odd-length KV rows.

ash: OK plan: 1) Sam adds CI test, 2) Maria bisects pack util change and uploads reproable minimal patch, 3) Kevin reviews kernel rotary precision paths for quant4->int accum cast differences, 4) if root cause is pack util, revert or patch for correctness then re-optimize later.

sam: I started the CI test PR: https://repo.internal/redwood/ci/pull/1292 — it runs on a single GPU runner and compares logits L2 norm between modes.

maria: Also note context window limit behavior: when we hit soft limit near 64k the prefill path trims older tokens and rewrites KV; incremental path drops at different boundary which produced mismatched index mapping. So we need to ensure eviction policy is identical between codepaths.

kevin: Good catch. I'll add an invariant check: after any eviction, assert that kv.index_map == replayed_prefill.index_map in debug builds. If mismatch, log full map.

ash: I'll audit rotary table generation: ensure both prefill and incremental call the same sin/cos generator with identical dtype and seed. Also check quant kernel math that computes rotary scaling uses per-layer consistent dtype.

maria: For immediate unblock, running experiments: 
- revert pack util change (local) -> passes goldset for incremental
- run pack util with safer tail copy -> reduces divergence
- fp16 kernels -> eliminates divergence but costlier

sam: If revert is safe perf-wise we can ship revert + CI test, then reintroduce optimized pack util behind a runtime flag after correctness validated.

maria: Agreed. I'll make a minimal revert PR and link it here.

ci-bot: PR created: https://repo.internal/redwood/infra/pull/3401 by maria — revert pack-util-tail-optimization for correctness

kevin: I'll run a quick perf comparison to quantify regression. If it's <5% throughput drop we can accept revert.

ash: Also add a small numeric tolerance check in our eval harness so we avoid flapping on micro-diffs that don't affect user-facing quality. But keep the CI test strict for regressions beyond that.

maria: Will follow up with logs and the minimal bisect. Thanks all :rocket: 

sam: tagging @infra-oncall just in case rolling revert touches shared kernels.

kevin: ping me once PR is up on staging, I'll run long-run 24h sanity.

maria: PR merged to staging, starting long-run. Last note: the divergence seems to correlate with certain token alignments (when a long ASCII run crosses a 1024-token boundary). Might be a pathological tail case. I'll include that token pattern in the goldset.
